content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Payments demand is well above forecast: 112 calls against 65 expected at 09:15 (+72%). Service level fell to 49% with 14 abandons. The rise is spread across most payment reasons: refund_status x1.53, upi_payment_failed x1.46, payment_status_enquiry x1.39 and other_payments x1.30. Supply-side causes are ruled out. AHT is in line with forecast, so this is not system slowness. Absences are at or below normal, so this is not a sick wave. The only open incident is a P4 internal email delay with no customer impact, so no outage is confirmed. The 08:35 UPI cashback push does not explain the pattern well. The 08:00 interval was already +46% before the push. Refund and status enquiries rose as much as UPI calls. Offer enquiries are actually down. Because no cause is established, this is an unknown demand surge. General queue is roughly on forecast (-4%).","plan_name":"Payments surge recovery: break shift, coaching cancel, staged overtime, digital deflection and callback","rationale":"At about 300 s AHT, payments is short by roughly 10-13 agents at current volume. The plan uses free levers first, then targeted paid ones. (1) Delay payments breaks in the 09:30-11:00 peak by 30 minutes, which borrows capacity now. (2) Cancel non-mandatory payments coaching until 13:00 to return agents to phones (Rs 150 per session hour). (3) Offer overtime in two consecutive blocks starting 10:00, since agents arrive 30 minutes after approval. Expect about 8 acceptances for 10:00-12:00 and 6 for 12:00-14:00, roughly Rs 10,080, within the Rs 15,000 budget. (4) Deflect up to 20% of refund_status and payment_status_enquiry calls to chat. These are the two largest rising reasons and suit digital handling; estimated cost is about Rs 2,000-2,500. (5) Offer callbacks on payments for waits over 120 s, to protect against abandons while overtime ramps up. No cross-skilled agents are moved from general. It runs at about 21 Erlangs on 24 agents, so moving agents would risk pushing it below 70%. No outage message is used because no outage is confirmed.
